entries.07b18f82a6c5f65b: Revenue for the fiscal year ended December 2025 was ¥8,191,248 thousand (up 50.6% year on year); the securities report attributes this to an increase in properties handled and in the number of property sales, driven by the expansion of sales staff. The number of purchase settlements and the number of sales, which the company regards as key management indicators, were 1,533 and 1,506 respectively in the second half of the fiscal year ended December 2025 (July to December), up from 1,051 and 1,026 in the first half (January to June). The business risks section of the securities report states that, owing to the nature of the commission-based bonus system for sales staff, deliveries tend to concentrate in the final month of the second and fourth quarters, most notably December.

entries.0a2c6c6581c0a91f: Gross profit for the fiscal year ended December 2025 was ¥4,479,203 thousand (up 84.7% year on year), operating profit was ¥1,311,446 thousand (up 137.2%), ordinary profit was ¥1,263,449 thousand (up 142.1%), and net income was ¥981,647 thousand (up 159.6%). Selling, general and administrative expenses were ¥3,167,756 thousand (up 69.2% year on year), and the securities report states that this was due to increased personnel costs and advertising expenses accompanying the expansion of staff. The business risks section states that purchase funds are raised from the company's own capital and borrowings from financial institutions, and that its dependence on interest-bearing debt is relatively high. Inventory at the end of December 2025 was ¥901 million.

entries.45a9184943952d6e: Transactions in which real estate such as vacant houses bought from sellers is sold to buyers. They are mainly sales of income-producing real estate, detached houses, and condominium units, and revenue is recognized when the property is delivered to the buyer. It is the largest of the categories into which revenue from external customers is divided, for the fiscal year ended December 2025. The securities report states that holding purchased properties as inventory ties up funds and requires registration-related costs and inventory management, so the Company reduces this burden by using contracts for the benefit of a third party (sanni transactions). In a sanni transaction, the seller and the business operator, and the business operator and the buyer, each enter into a sales contract, so registration of ownership in the operator's name is not required and the property is not held as inventory.

entries.a278dff3e805c0ff: In May 2019, Kenji Kawata, the current representative director, and Hayato Uchikiba, a former co-representative, took over all shares of Room Select Co., Ltd. and conducted a capital increase. In connection with this, it changed its company name to the current AlbaLink Co., Ltd., changed its representative to Kenji Kawata, and relocated its head office to Fukuzumi, Koto Ward, Tokyo. At the same time, it changed its business format to the real estate purchase and resale business.
entries.a3d9475989873c87: A category of real estate-related transactions that fall under neither real estate sale and purchase transactions nor fee-based takeover transactions. The notes on revenue recognition divide revenue from external customers into three categories: real estate sale and purchase transactions, fee-based takeover transactions and other real estate-related transactions. In the sales results table of the securities report, the MD&A groups fee-based takeover transactions, real estate rental, vacation rental operation and others together as "Other Real Estate-Related." The company started the vacation rental business as a new business in May 2025. This category is a product and service category presented separately in the securities report, not a reportable segment.

entries.a8d4e60ba8e577af: A transaction type in which the company receives money from the seller and takes over the real estate. The securities report states that for properties that are difficult even for the company to purchase because of land prices, building condition and other factors, when there is demand from a buyer, the company may undertake paid consulting on disposing of the property and ultimately purchase it, which in substance amounts to a fee-based takeover. The company is a member of the Real Estate Fee-Based Takeover Council, which aims to improve the soundness of the fee-based real estate takeover industry, and conducts transactions in accordance with its self-regulatory rules. It was included in "Other Real Estate-Related Transactions" in the previous fiscal year, but because its monetary importance has grown, it has been presented separately since the fiscal year ended December 2025.

entries.d0f1f62ab9d17fb5: The company buys vacant houses from sellers and sells them to buyers. The securities report states that the company accumulates information on how buyers renovate properties after purchase, what rent they set and how much income they earn, and that by estimating the property price buyers expect, it can promptly appraise how much to buy from sellers. For properties that are difficult to buy, where there is buyer demand, the company undertakes disposal consulting for a fee and also carries out paid takeovers, in which it ultimately purchases the property itself. From May 2025, the company also started a minpaku business using the properties it purchased.
entries.d3b702163d89a3c3: The [[term:annual-securities-report|annual securities report]] states that, under the mission of "Zero vacant houses in 2100", the company operates a vacant house matching business across Japan, buying vacant houses from vacant house owners (sellers) gathered mainly through its own WEB media and selling them to buyers who want to make use of vacant houses. In principle, rather than acting as an intermediary, it takes the form of the company buying and selling, so it can secure revenue without being subject to the cap on brokerage fees, but a burden of holding inventory arises, so it uses san-i transactions, in which it clearly states that it will sell to the buyer and the seller and the buyer each enter into a contract, to reduce inventory. Net sales for the fiscal year ended December 2025 were ¥8,191,248 thousand (up 50.6% year on year). There is no customer accounting for 10% or more of net sales.
entries.d46c1f68104ca805: This business buys vacant houses from owners who want to dispose of them (sellers) and sells them to buyers who want to make use of them (purchasers); it is the company's single segment. From the fiscal year ended December 2025, the segment name was changed from 'Real Estate Business' to 'Vacant House Matching Business'. The securities report states that it mainly gathers sellers through its own WEB media, conducts in-person appraisals at branches nationwide, and in principle buys and resells properties rather than acting as an intermediary. Revenue for the fiscal year ended December 2025 was ¥8,191,248 thousand (up 50.6% year on year), and operating profit was ¥1,311,446 thousand (up 137.2% year on year). The securities report attributes the increase in revenue to a rise in the number of properties handled as the sales staff expanded, which increased the number of property sales.
